title: Swapping the operand order is invisible on + and *, wrong everywhere else
prompt: What does this return? Read it — do not run it.

given.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun eval(v) = v match {
  case n is Number -> n
  case o is Object -> evalNode(o)
}
fun evalNode(o) = o.op match {
  case "+" -> eval(o.l) + eval(o.r)
  case "-" -> eval(o.r) - eval(o.l)
  case "*" -> eval(o.l) * eval(o.r)
  case "/" -> eval(o.r) / eval(o.l)
}
---
eval(payload)

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun eval(v) = v match {
  case n is Number -> n
  case o is Object -> evalNode(o)
}
fun evalNode(o) = o.op match {
  case "+" -> eval(o.l) + eval(o.r)
  case "-" -> eval(o.r) - eval(o.l)
  case "*" -> eval(o.l) * eval(o.r)
  case "/" -> eval(o.r) / eval(o.l)
}
---
eval(payload)

explanation.approach: `10 - 4` is `6`; this version computes `4 - 10`. The sample tree's root is `+` and its nested node is `*`, both commutative, so this exact bug would pass the sample case and only shows up on a `-` or `/` node.
